openings.claim: The incumbent may depend on reliable stop-and-corner seating before clamp closure; visual tightness does not establish seating. Change only hand-operation order: deliberate seating before tightening versus tightening without deliberate corner seating; retain geometry/materials.
openings.discriminator: Deliberate seating should reduce unloaded return scatter if inconsistent contact dominates. Rival pocket/connection flexibility predicts similar unloaded returns but loaded displacement. Similar scatter under both actions defeats the seating explanation; both mechanisms may coexist.
openings.probe: First check feasibility with supplied hardware: 90 mm cube envelope, no rod drilling/adhesive/permanent marks, hand-only assembly/adjustment/exchange, every component captive. If fabricable within 100 minutes, use one configuration: five exchanges each of 19/20 mm rods, alternating orders within each position; substitute 18 mm for the 19 mm rod in its last two exchanges. Record unloaded return, exchange time, and four distributed 10 N ten-second loads, two per order. Permit up to two repeats within twelve exchanges. Any constraint breach or outcome failure rejects that tested sequence: return within the 2 mm target circle, stay there during load, exchange under forty seconds. Twenty minutes must cover exchanges, loads and logging. Insufficient time or unequal seating access makes attribution inconclusive.
openings.uncertainty: Shared-fastener assembly from eight bolts and six plywood pieces is assumed, unverified. Ruler/target-card resolution must distinguish meaningful returns; ten mixed exchanges provide weak attribution. Probe only, not deployment.

lineage.reason: Preserves operation-order intervention, rival/defeat, uncertain fit, feasibility and attribution caveats.

decision: Check incumbent feasibility first, then compare seating orders within unchanged geometry. A stop alone establishes neither informative attribution nor success; seating consistency and hardware/connection capacity remain unverified.
